subject: Sundial-mini onboarding & provisional pin request
messages:
From: Ashley Martin <ashley.martin@sundial.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sundial-mini: onboarding request + tokenizer concern

Hi Neha / Lauren / Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday on the discovery call. As discussed, Sundial would like Redwood to onboard our Sundial-mini model (sundial-mini-v1.2) for early customer trials. A couple of important notes up front:

- We discovered a tokenizer edge-case with some historical logs (attached tokenizer-diff.csv) where punctuation normalization differs for ~0.7% of our training corpus. That caused small but visible output drift in our internal QA.
- We need a provisional pin for the variant during the initial 2-week pilot so we can validate outputs against our golden prompts and run the tokenizer parity tests you run during intake.

Attached: onboarding manifest + security sheet. Can Redwood accept a temporary pin for sundial-mini-v1.2 while compatibility checks run? If so, what form should the request take (formal PR, intake ticket, or a signed addendum)?

Procurement note: procurement@sundial.ai will follow up if you need an MSA amendment for provisional SLAs.

Appreciate a quick run-of-play and any blockers from your side.

Cheers,
Ashley Martin
Head of Platform Partnerships
Sundial AI
Ashley.Martin@sundial.ai

Attachments: sundial-onboarding-manifest.json (manifest), sundial-security-sheet.pdf (security questionnaire), tokenizer-diff.csv (sample diffs)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Ashley Martin <ashley.martin@sundial.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sundial-mini: onboarding request + tokenizer concern

Ashley, thanks — and welcome.

High-level yes: we can do a provisional variant pin while running compatibility and safety checks, but we need to lock down the scope and acceptance criteria. Proposed next steps from our side:

1) Intake ticket (I'll open RDW-5483) with the manifest you attached and a clear list of golden prompts and regression checks.
2) Temporary pin window: default is 14 days from intake acceptance, extendable with sign-off from product and safety.
3) Technical compatibility tests: tokenizer parity, KV-cache validation, and a short perf baseline (latency/throughput) on the target Dedicated profile. Karthik — can you confirm ETA for a tokenizer parity run and whether we need a dev artifact from Sundial beyond the diff CSV?
4) Product acceptance: we need 10 golden prompts + scoring rubric so we can run quality monitoring during the pin window. Priyom — can you pair with Sundial on the eval harness?

If procurement needs a formal addendum for provisional SLA guarantees, send their contact and we will get legal looped in. Also, please confirm whether sundial-mini-v1.2 is intended to be the default variant or if you want it behind an explicit route.

I'll attach the intake checklist link in the intake ticket and flag product + infra canaries.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Partnerships (Onboarding)
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Ashley / Neha — quick technical update from infra/runtime:

- Tokenizer parity: thanks for the diff CSV. We'll run a parity job against our canonical tokenizer (BPE v4 safe-normalize) and generate a 2000-sample mismatch report; estimate 36h once we have a packaged tokenizer artifact (preferred: wheel or small Docker image with the tokenizer binary). If Sundial can't provide a package, we can still run a blind diff with your CSV but it's higher friction.
- KV-cache and cache-compat: we expect no architectural changes for a 7B-class model, but we'll validate KV shapes and serialization.
- Pin semantics: we support a soft pin via our intake config that prevents automatic variant replacement by newer model imports. For a hard pin that prevents even manual rollforward you'd need product + legal sign-off.

Can Sundial provide: (a) tokenizer artifact or build instructions, (b) confirmation of expected max-sequence-length, (c) whether PEFT adapters are in use (if yes, include adapter metadata). With that I can queue the tests and give a concrete ETA.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Hi Neha / Karthik / team — thanks for the quick turnaround.

Responses inline:
- Tokenizer artifact: we can provide a small wheel with the tokenizer (attached in a follow-up secure link) — will share today. If you prefer Docker we can do that instead.
- Max sequence length: 2048 (default).
- PEFT: no adapters for this release.
- Golden prompts + rubric: attached to procurement message; I'll paste a short list into the intake ticket once it's open.

Procurement note: procurement@sundial.ai will send the provisional SLA addendum doc to legal if required. We are OK with a 14-day provisional pin window; if you can provide the soft pin in intake, we'll follow up with formal sign-off for a hard pin if the trial looks good.

Thanks — Ashley
Ashley Martin
Head of Platform Partnerships, Sundial AI
